note: Twin candidates considered and rejected. Kept so the same candidate is not proposed twice.

rejected.proposed_as: a within-problem twin of case 6: the Guth-Katz method was believed not to transfer to R^3, which would have made R^3 a clean negative.
rejected.rejected_because: A search this session found a recent paper (arXiv:2608.14454) claiming the Erdos distinct distances problem in R^3 up to a subpolynomial factor, proving N^{2/3-o(1)}. Prior to it the best was Solymosi-Vu bootstrapping to N^{3/5}/log^{2/5} N. The landscape moved, so 'still open in R^3' is no longer true and the item is not a negative.
rejected.lesson: Twin candidates decay. Every twin needs a re-check date, not just a citation.
